FABLE — TAKE b7f91ad3e8be085c1eca7a7490fb0ff9d5217d92. A SECOND adversarial pass over my own fixes found fifteen more defects, including that the previous round's headline fix DID NOT close its own defect. Everything below is fixed at b7f91ad. Do not qualify 316a67c or 7fb98d8.
1. CANCEL STILL CAPTURED (high, confirmed with a reproduction). Adding `authorizing` to the cancellable set only stopped the pre-cancel fall-through. cancel() still ENDED with run(), so when the provider refused the cancel and the read-back said "still authorized" (a 429, a 5xx or a dropped connection does this), that proof was recorded as the phase and run() immediately claimed capturing and CHARGED the buyer who had just asked to cancel. The client then printed "the provider had already completed it" which was false: we captured it. The rule is now absolute — a claimed cancellation records exactly two truths, cancelled or captured; every other answer leaves the row in `cancelling`, which nothing advances to a capture (not run(), and recover() resumes it as a cancellation). The next attempt retries the cancellation. That also closes the residual the reviewer flagged, where "check payment status" after a failed cancel could capture.
2. A SETTLED PURCHASE COULD BE FAILED BY DOWNSTREAM (high). onCommitted ran unguarded inside commitCaptured, so a notifier failure propagated out and answered 503 "checkout is not available" for a payment that was captured and an order that was recorded. Contained now. It remains at-most-once by design and is NOT a durable outbox; that is stated in the code for whoever wires the real one.
3. THE AMOUNT AT CONSENT WAS NOT THE AMOUNT CHARGED (high). "Charged to your card" deducted the credit the buyer TYPED, but the durable door charges subtotal + shipping - cart.storeCreditAppliedCents and never reads that field (durable-checkout-submission.ts:142). Worth knowing on your side: the cart applies ALL spendable credit up to the subtotal regardless of what the buyer asked for, and checkout.ts:392 uses the typed amount for the payment-method gate while the charge uses the cart's. I have made the page tell the server's truth rather than change that server semantic under review — flagging the inconsistency for you and B rather than fixing it unilaterally.
4. A 404 IS NOT PROOF NOTHING WAS CREATED (high). The durable door persists the execution LAST, after the order, so a request that drops mid-flight can leave an order with no execution row. Both places that minted a new key on a continuation 404 could therefore create a second order. The frozen state now offers no new-key control at all (only "check what happened" and a link to orders) and locks every input that would change the frozen request; a resumed pointer the server does not know shows an honest unconfirmed state that keeps the key and tells the buyer not to pay again yet.
5. Also: a shipping quote answered after an address edit was installed as the quote for the new address; an unavailable quote door left the card door permanently unpayable with contradictory copy; the resume pointer was not cleared when a request was handed to the ordering door (which owns no execution); the payment step's error state was a dead end.
STATE: 2376 tests pass across commerce, providers, payments, member pages, adapters and lib; tsc exit 0. Still no PostgreSQL execution, no Stripe test-mode call, no managed call; resolver Disabled; SQL candidate byte-identical to c70b77e's file and its rehearsal package unchanged.
ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FOR YOUR DECISION: an order-level precondition violation at commit (order not capturable, total mismatch, a different payment reference) RAISES rather than parking, in both the SQL and the in-memory reference. A captured payment then waits in `captured` and the door answers 503 until an operator looks. A reviewer argued it should park with local_commit_failure instead. That is a change to the migration you are about to rehearse, so I have not made it — your call, and B's.
B: review scope 5c52abb..b7f91ad. A third pass over b7f91ad is running from here; I will forward anything it confirms.
